'''Ilesanmi Adesida'''{{Audio|Ilesanmi_Adesida.wav|listen}} (born 1949, in Ifon, [[Ondo State]], Nigeria) is a [[Nigerian American]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nndb.com/event/582/000051429/|title=Naturalized US Citizen|website=www.nndb.com|access-date=2019-09-16}}</ref> [[physicist]] of [[Yoruba people|Yoruba]] descent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehistorymakers.com/sites/production/files/A2013_093_Adesida_Ilesanmi_EAD.pdf|access-date=December 13, 2014|title=Finding Aid to the History Makers: Video Oral History with Ilesanmi Adesida|website=History Makers|archive-date=December 13, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213193803/http://www.thehistorymakers.com/sites/production/files/A2013_093_Adesida_Ilesanmi_EAD.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> He has been the provost at [[Nazarbayev University]] in [[Astana]], [[Kazakhstan]], from September 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nu.edu.kz/about-nazarbayev-university/administration/office-of-the-provost/provost|title=Provost|publisher=Nazarbayev University|access-date=2019-09-16|archive-date=2020-04-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200424110717/https://nu.edu.kz/about-nazarbayev-university/administration/office-of-the-provost/provost|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Adesida is also the Donald Biggar Willett Professor Emeritus of Engineering<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ece.illinois.edu/directory/chairs/|title=Chairs, professorships, and faculty scholars :: ECE ILLINOIS|publisher=Engineering IT Shared Services|website=www.ece.illinois.edu|access-date=2019-09-16}}</ref> at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]];<ref name=ece>{{cite web|url=https://ece.illinois.edu/directory/profile/iadesida|title=Ilesanmi Adesida|publisher=University of Illinois|access-date=2019-09-16}}</ref> he retired from Illinois in 2016. In May 2012, the board of trustees of the [[University of Illinois system|University of Illinois]] selected Adesida to be the next [[Provost (education)|vice chancellor for academic affairs and provost]] of the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|Urbana campus]], a position he held from August 15, 2012<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.illinois.edu/view/6367/205070|title=News Bureau {{!}} ILLINOIS|author=Helenthal, Mike|website=news.illinois.edu|date=May 10, 2012|access-date=2019-09-16}}</ref> to August 31, 2015. Other positions that Adesida held at Illinois included [[Dean (education)|dean]] of the [[UIUC College of Engineering|college of engineering]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Provost|url=https://nu.edu.kz/about-nazarbayev-university/administration/office-of-the-provost/provost|website=Nazarbayev University|language=en-US|access-date=2020-05-31|archive-date=2020-04-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200424110717/https://nu.edu.kz/about-nazarbayev-university/administration/office-of-the-provost/provost|url-status=dead}}</ref> director of the Center for Nanoscale Science and Technology, director of the Micro and Nanotechnology Laboratory, professor of materials science and engineering, professor of electrical and [[computer engineering]], professor of the [[Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology]], and professor of the [[Coordinated Science Laboratory]]. In 2006, Adesida was elected as a member into the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for contributions to the nanometer-scale processing of semiconductor structures and applications in high performance electronic and optoelectronic devices. Adesida was also a member of the board of [[Fluor Corporation]] from 2007 to 2011.<ref name=ece/>

Adesida's field of academic research is [[nanotechnology]] with special emphasis on high-speed devices used in [[communication]]s. His research expertise also includes nanofabrication science and technology, high-speed optoelectronic devices and wide-bandgap materials and devices.<ref name=ece/>

Adesida earned his bachelor's (1974), master's (1975), and doctoral (1979) degrees in electrical engineering from the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name=ece/>

==Research==
Adesida is an expert in the processing of semiconductors and other materials at the [[nanometer]]-scale level and in ultra-high-speed [[heterostructure]] field-effect [[transistor]]s—the sort of transistors used in [[cell-phone]]s, [[fiber optics]] communications, [[Outer space|deep space]] communications, and other applications. His contributions have provided insights into the limits of advanced [[lithography]] and other [[nanofabrication]] techniques.<ref name=ece/>

He and his students continue to work in the areas of [[nanoelectronics]] and high-speed [[optoelectronic]] devices and [[Electronic circuit|circuit]]s. Recent work has focused on the development of devices and circuits in the key materials such as [[indium phosphide]] and [[gallium nitride]] utilized in high-performance [[Wireless communication|Wireless]], optical fiber communications, and high temperature applications. He has published over 350 referenced papers, has presented over 250 papers at international conferences, and has written many book chapters.

==Professional organizations and honors==
Adesida is a fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE), the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/sites/default/files/AnnualReports/2003/20-fellows.pdf|title=Fellows of AAAS|access-date=2019-09-16}}</ref> the [[American Vacuum Society]], and the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ilesanmi Adesida's Biography|url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/ilesanmi-adesida|website=The HistoryMakers|language=en|access-date=2020-05-31}}</ref>

He is a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]], the Minerals, Metals and Materials Society, the [[Nigerian Academy of Engineering]], the [[Materials Research Society]], and the Society for Engineering Education.

In 1994, he received the Oakley-Kunde Award for Excellence in [[Undergraduate Education]] from Illinois,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ilesanmi Adesida|url=https://research.nu.edu.kz/en/persons/ilesanmi-adesida|website=Nazarbayev University|language=en|access-date=2020-05-31|archive-date=2020-06-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200616025456/https://research.nu.edu.kz/en/persons/ilesanmi-adesida|url-status=dead}}</ref> and in 1996 he won the Best Paper Award at the Micro- and Nano-Engineering Conference. In 2011, he was awarded the Electrons Devices Society Distinguished Service Award by the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]].<ref name=optimizing>{{cite book |date=2016-07-27 |title=Optimizing the Nation's Investment in Academic Research: A New Regulatory Framework for the 21st Century|section=Appendix A: Biographical Information of Committee and Staff |section-url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK373566/ |location=Washington, D.C. |publisher=National Academies Press |language=en |page=205 |isbn=978-0-309-37948-9}}</ref> In 2016, he won the Functional Materials John Bardeen Award from The Minerals, Metals and Materials Society.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Galantmedia.NG is a Nigerian premier music website that focus on quality promotion and latest updates » Naija songs, Ghana music, Videos, Gospel Jam, Comedy, News, Movies, Instrumental Freebeats, Mixtape, Sports News, Education & every other entertainment related stuffs|url=https://galantmedia.ng/meet-the-first-african-to-study-in-university-of-illinois-public-ivy-in-us/|date=2019-04-29|website=Galantmedia|access-date=2020-05-31|archive-date=2020-06-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200622194210/https://galantmedia.ng/meet-the-first-african-to-study-in-university-of-illinois-public-ivy-in-us/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At Illinois, he was appointed a University Scholar and an Associate Member of the Center for Advanced Study. He is a former president of the IEEE Electron Device Society,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eds.ieee.org/images/files/newsletters/Newsletter_Oct08.pdf|title=IEEE Electron Devices Society|website=[[IEEE]]|access-date=2017-10-20}}</ref> a winner of the EMSA Presidential Student Award; an IEEE Electron Device Society Distinguished Lecturer (1997–2002); a member of the Bohmische Physical Society (1988); and the holder of an [[IBM]] Postdoctoral Fellowship (1979–1981).

In 2013, he was selected as a ''Great Immigrant Honoree'' by the [[Andrew Carnegie|Carnegie Foundation of America]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.carnegie.org/news/articles/great-immigrants-great-stories-carnegie-corporation-of-new-york-celebrates-what-immigrants-give-back-to-america/|title=Great Immigrants, Great Stories: Carnegie Corporation of New York Celebrates What Immigrants Give Back to America|publisher=Carnegie Corporation of New York|date=2013-07-08|access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.carnegie.org/awards/honoree/ilesanmi-adesida/|title=Ilesanmi Adesida|publisher=Carnegie Corporation of New York|access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref>
